data.raw_text:
Lieutenant Edward Max Price gave his life in service aboard the aircraft carrier USS
Lexington (CV-2) during the Battle of the Coral Sea on May 8, 1942. He was just 25 years old.
Born June 20, 1916, in Charleston, West Virginia, to John and Mary Price, Edward built an early reputation for discipline and academic excellence. After graduating from Hargrave Military Academy and studying at Concord College, he earned an appointment to the United States Naval Academy as part of the Class of 1939—where he would go on to achieve the top academic standing among his peers.
Following his commissioning as an Ensign, Price was assigned to the USS Lexington.
By the spring of 1942, he had risen to the role of gunnery officer, responsible for directing the ship's defensive firepower during one of the Pacific War's earliest and most critical naval battles.

On the morning of May 8, Japanese aircraft launched a fierce assault against the Lexington. Amid the chaos of bombs and torpedoes striking the carrier, Lt. Price remained at his post, continuing to direct anti-aircraft fire. In the heat of battle, while urging his crew to keep up the tight, he was struck and killed by shrapnel from an exploding bomb.
The Lexington, ravaged by fire and damage, was ultimately abandoned and deliberately sunk later that day. In total, 216 sailors were lost.
Lt. Price's body was never recovered.
Today, his name is honored among the missing at the Manila American Cemetery.
His bravery was formally recognized with words that speak to both his skill and his courage: he played a vital role in defending the ship by expertly coordinating its guns and remained at his station until the very end, upholding the finest traditions of naval service.

He was one of 79 graduates from the Naval Academy's Class of 1939 who would not return home.
Stories like his carry a personal weight, especially when they echo the service of loved ones-like a father who wore the uniform of the Marine Corps, and an uncle who served in the Navy. Different paths, same quiet commitment to something greater than themselves. 🙏🇺🇸🙏
